'''Sangu Shrine''' (山宮神社, *Sangu Jinja*) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located at Shichikama, Shin'onsen, Mikata District, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|qid=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture}}. It was formerly classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The main deity enshrined is {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇命}}, with additional enshrinements of {{ill|Izanagi|en|Izanagi|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi}}, {{ill|Izanami|en|Izanami|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami}}, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|誉田別尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Homuda Wake no Mikoto|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=応神天皇|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q317997}}, and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|スサノオノミコト}}.

== Overview ==
The shrine is located atop a small forested hill near the source of the {{ill|Shichikama Onsen|ja|七釜温泉|qid=Q11353724}}. The exact founding date is unknown. Before the modern era, it was known as '''Sangami Gongen''' (山神権現). In {{ill|1868|en|1868|qid=Q7717|lt=1868}} (the first year of the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}), it was renamed to its current title. In {{ill|1873|en|1873|qid=Q7757|lt=1873}} (Meiji 6), it was designated a village shrine and enshrined {{ill|Hachiman|en|Hachiman|qid=Q261637|lt=Hachiman}} and the local {{ill|Placenta deity|ja|胞衣神}}.

The shrine's main hall was rebuilt in {{ill|1444|en|1444|qid=Q6420|lt=1444}} (Bun'an 1, {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}}), but was destroyed in {{ill|1944|en|1944|qid=Q5268|lt=1944}} (Shōwa 19) due to a typhoon. The current structure was rebuilt after World War II.

== Festivals and Events ==
* Annual Festival: September 29<ref>{{Cite web|title=Festival Calendar - Sangu Shrine|url=https://www.kirinnomachi-japan-heritage.jp/jp/reisai/1059/|access-date=2022-12-19|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}</ref>

== Cultural Properties ==
* '''Shichikama {{ill|Qilin dance|ja|麒麟獅子舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kirin Shishi-mai|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=麒麟獅子|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11677329}} Dance''' - Town-designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property (designated March 31, 1986)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shichikama Kirin Shishi-mai|url=https://www.town.shinonsen.hyogo.jp/page/?mode=detail&page_id=8ab359199e3f3c495d46db6ceb3791ec|access-date=2022-12-19|publisher=Shin'onsen Town}}</ref>
* '''Sangu Shrine Sacred Forest''' (山宮神社社叢) - Town-designated Natural Monument (designated March 31, 1986), featuring ancient {{ill|Castanopsis sieboldii|en|Castanopsis sieboldii|qid=Q846994|lt=Castanopsis}} and {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|en|Chamaecyparis obtusa|qid=Q917187|lt=Hinoki cypress}} trees, along with thick growths of {{ill|Camellia japonica|ja|ヤブツバキ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Camellia japonica|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=ツバキ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q160121}} and {{ill|Cleyera japonica|en|Cleyera japonica|qid=Q775470|lt=Sakaki}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sacred Forest of Shichikama Sangu Shrine|url=https://www.town.shinonsen.hyogo.jp/page/?mode=detail&page_id=b500773414376fa6bd4970ec294860e2|access-date=2022-12-19|publisher=Shin'onsen Town}}</ref>

== Access ==
* {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|arz|شركة سكك حديد غرب اليابان|azb|باتی ژاپون دمیریول‌لاری|ca|Companyia de Ferrocarrils del Japó Occidental|cs|JR West|da|West Japan Railway Company|de|West Japan Railway Company|eo|JR Okcidenta|es|West Japan Railway Company|fa|شرکت راه‌آهن غرب ژاپن|fi|JR Nishi-Nihon|fr|West Japan Railway Company|hu|West Japan Railway Company|id|Perusahaan Kereta Api Jepang Barat|it|West Japan Railway Company|ja|西日本旅客鉄道|jv|West Japan Railway Company|ko|서일본 여객철도|ms|Syarikat Kereta Api Jepun Barat|nds|JR Westjapan|nl|West Japan Railway Company|pl|West Japan Railway Company|pt|West Japan Railway Company|ru|West Japan Railway Company|sv|JR Nishi Nihon|th|บริษัทรถไฟญี่ปุ่นตะวันตก|tl|West Japan Railway Company|tr|West Japan Railway Company|uk|West Japan Railway Company|ur|ویسٹ جاپان ریلوے کمپنی|wuu|西日本旅客铁道|zh|西日本旅客鐵道|zh_min_nan|Se Ji̍t-pún Lú-kheh Thih-tō|zh_yue|西日本旅客鐵道|qid=Q502125|lt=West Japan Railway Company}} (JR West) {{ill|San'in Main Line|en|San'in Main Line|qid=Q1135170|lt=San'in Main Line}}: From {{ill|Hamasaka Station|en|Hamasaka Station|qid=Q872032|lt=Hamasaka Station}}, take the {{ill|Zentan Bus|ja|全但バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zentan Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11389110}} bound for {{ill|Q11563591|ja|湯村温泉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yumura Onsen (Hyōgo)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11563591}}, and get off at "Shichikama Onsen-guchi" bus stop. 5-minute walk.
* From Osaka or Kobe, take the Zentan Bus {{ill|Zentan Bus|ja|夢千代号|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yumechiyo-go|ja_comment=fixed jawiki redirect|3=全但バス|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11389110}} to "Yumura Onsen," transfer to the bus for Hamasaka, and get off at "Shichikama Onsen-guchi." 5-minute walk.
